content:
I should ask the user directly which license they want—MIT, Apache-2.0, or GPL-3.0—and also get the copyright holder name, offering a few concrete options like their username or project name plus an "Other" choice.

A third question can cover whether to commit and push the changes with updated GitHub metadata, keep everything local for review, or open a PR instead—bundling all three into one call is efficient since the license choice affects package.json and README badges anyway, so it's worth asking upfront before doing the dependent work.

item.text: I've got a clear picture of the repo: a BB plugin (TypeScript, 8 passing tests, clean typecheck), public on GitHub, 2 commits, no license, no CI, no topics, and no repo metadata in `package.json`. Two quick decisions before I make the changes:

questions.question: Which license should I add to bb-thread-reference?

options.label: MIT (Recommended)
options.description: Short, permissive, the default for BB/Claude plugins and most npm packages. Maximum adoption, no patent clause.
options.preview:
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2026 <holder>

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy...

options.label: Apache-2.0
options.description: Permissive like MIT but adds an explicit patent grant and requires stating changes. Longer file; preferred by some companies.

options.label: GPL-3.0
options.description: Copyleft: anyone distributing a derivative must open-source it under GPL too. Limits commercial/closed reuse of the plugin.

questions.question: What name should appear as the copyright holder?

options.label: Tom (MacHatter1)
options.description: Matches your git author name and GitHub handle on the existing commits.

options.label: acme
options.description: Attributes copyright to the organisation behind your email domain rather than to you personally.

questions.question: How far should I take the changes on GitHub itself?

options.label: Commit + push + repo settings (Recommended)
options.description: Commit to main, push to origin, and set repo topics/homepage via gh. Fastest path to a polished public repo.

options.label: Commit locally, don't push
options.description: I make and commit all file changes; you review and push yourself. No remote changes at all.

options.label: Push as a pull request
options.description: Work lands on a branch and I open a PR against main so you can review the diff on GitHub before merging.
